title: 38yo M Traumatic Hand Amputation
chiefComplaint: Hand caught in a sugarcane cutting machine
background: Sugarcane harvester, injured 90 minutes ago when he reached into a jammed cutting drum without shutting it off. His co-workers wrapped the stump in a shirt and drove him in on a tractor trailer. The amputated part was retrieved and is loose in a plastic bag with ice water directly against the tissue, which is the wrong way to transport it. He is right hand dominant and this is his right hand. He has no formal employment contract and no compensation cover.

exam.finding: Alert, grey, sweating, holding the wrapped stump above his head as instructed by a co-worker, remarkably calm in the way that severe pain and adrenaline sometimes produce
Pale conjunctivae, dry lips, no head injury, no facial trauma, speaking in full sentences
Sinus tachycardia at 118/min, blood pressure maintained, capillary refill 3 seconds in the uninjured hand, brachial and radial pulses present on the injured arm
Clear chest, tachypnoeic from pain and anxiety, no chest trauma
Soft and non-tender, no other injury found on secondary survey, no seatbelt or handlebar mark

Amputation through the metacarpals with ragged crushed edges and contaminated cane fibre and soil in the wound. Bleeding is now venous ooze rather than arterial spurt. Forearm swollen and tense to mid-forearm with pain on passive finger extension of the remaining digits
GCS 15. Median and ulnar sensory distribution absent distal to the wrist. Thumb and index remain attached but are pale, cold and capillary refill is over 5 seconds

investigations.name: Haemoglobin
investigations.report: Moderate acute anaemia from field blood loss. Group and crossmatch 4 units.

investigations.name: X-ray right hand and forearm
investigations.report: Transmetacarpal amputation through the shafts of the second to fifth metacarpals with comminution. Radius and ulna intact. Radio-opaque debris in the soft tissues. Comminution over a long segment is the finding that predicts replantation will fail.

investigations.name: Creatine kinase
investigations.report: Rising, from crushed muscle. Watch renal function and start fluids.

investigations.name: INR and platelets
investigations.report: Normal. No coagulopathy yet, which is favourable for surgery.

investigations.name: Creatinine and potassium
investigations.report: Normal baseline. Repeat after reperfusion or fasciotomy, when potassium can rise abruptly.

data.label: Direct pressure and elevation, no blind clamping
actions: Direct pressure with a bulky dressing

doseMap.Tourniquet only if pressure fails: Windlass tourniquet proximal to the elbow, note the application time on the skin. Blind clamping in a bleeding field destroys the vessels and nerves a surgeon needs for repair

data.label: Correct storage of the amputated part
actions: Wrap the part in saline-moistened gauze
Place the bag on ice water, never the tissue directly on ice

doseMap.Place the bag on ice water, never the ti: Direct ice contact causes frostbite and ends any chance of replantation. Target 4 C. Warm ischaemia tolerance is about 6 hours, cold ischaemia about 12

doseMap.Morphine IV titrated: 2-4 mg IV every 5 min to effect
doseMap.Tetanus toxoid and immunoglobulin: Heavily contaminated agricultural wound, give both if immunisation status is unknown
doseMap.IV antibiotics: Cefazolin 2 g IV plus gentamicin, add penicillin for soil contamination and clostridial risk

data.label: Stabilised, but the forearm is worsening
data.narrative: Bleeding is controlled and the pain settles, but forearm compartment pressures are clinically high: tense swelling, pain on passive stretch, and progressive sensory loss in the remaining digits. Do not wait for a pressure measurement or for pulses to disappear. Pulses are the last sign and by then the muscle is dead.

data.label: Tell him honestly that replantation is unlikely, before he is anaesthetised (Empathy)
data.narrative: The co-workers have already told him the hospital will sew it back on. It is a crushed, contaminated, long-segment avulsion in his dominant hand and the honest probability of a functional replant is low. You tell him that yourself, in the resus room, while he can still ask questions. You also tell him what a functional prosthesis and hand therapy can realistically give him, and you get the social worker started on the compensation claim tonight rather than in a week. Pi Ek says the second half of that conversation is the part that determines whether he works again.

data.label: Urgent fasciotomy and theatre, do not wait for transfer
actions: Transfer discussion with the replantation centre

doseMap.Emergency forearm fasciotomy: Clinical diagnosis. Volar and dorsal incisions. A fasciotomy done unnecessarily costs a scar, a fasciotomy done late costs the forearm

data.label: Theatre findings
data.narrative: Fasciotomy releases tense but viable muscle. The replantation team declines the amputated part on the grounds of crush and contamination and performs a revision amputation with thumb preservation. Preserving the thumb is worth more functionally than any prosthesis.

data.label: Rhabdomyolysis prevention and rehabilitation planning
actions: IV fluids targeting urine output 1-2 mL/kg/h
Daily creatine kinase and renal function
Occupational compensation claim and social work

data.label: Disposition
data.narrative: Fasciotomy wounds closed on day 5. No renal failure. Discharged day 11. He has a functional thumb and a compensation claim in progress. He asks whether the machine will be fixed, and the honest answer is that the guard was removed two seasons ago because it slowed the harvest.
